newsitem.title: USA: American Standard amends Kelso plan.
newsitem.headline: American Standard amends Kelso plan.

text.p: American Standards Cos Inc on Friday released its 1996 results, showing operating income of $2.42 a share on consolidated sales of $5.8 billion, as part of an amendment to a plan by Kelso ASI Partners LP to exit its investment in the company.
The company also said it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Sorin Biomedica SpA to acquire Sorin's European medical diagnostics products business.
When an asset impairment charge of $235.2 million is included, the company posted a net loss in 1996 of $46.7 million, or $0.60 per share.
In the prior year, the company reported net income of $1.90 per share on consolidated sales of $5.2 billion.
American Standard said that its air conditioning products unit posted "strong results on higher sales and improved operating margin."

Its plumbing product results were "down primarily because of continued weak economic markets in Europe," it said. Its automotive products results also were down as a result of lower volume attributable to the decline in European commercial vehicle production, it said.
American Standard said it also has an agreement to acquire INCSTAR Corp, which is about 52 percent owned by Sorin.
Under the deal, INCSTAR shareholders would receive $6.32 a share in cash, and INCSTAR would become a wholly owned subsidiary.
American Standard said the Sorin and INCSTAR deals, which are expected to be completed in the first half of 1997, are valued at about $220 million.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
